problem_type: Canvas deletion was inferred from store snapshots and renderer project-file read-modify-write raced the main writer
symptom: Undoing a landed production batch detached shots without a reattach command, a signal from project A could be written into project B after a switch, and an external project edit could be overwritten by a late renderer delivery.
direct_cause: watchDeletedProductionNodes treated any loaded store node disappearance as a delete; production canvas signals omitted their owning project and the host used its current project for every signal; runProjectDelivery read and saved a whole project record in the renderer while the main gateway could write the same file.
class_root: User intent, signal project identity, and project-file write ownership were not enforced at shared boundaries: snapshot lifecycle was mistaken for deletion, signal delivery was bound to the current host instead of the emitting canvas store, and more than one process could own a read-modify-write.
affected_population: Production batches using undo/redo or delete/cut gestures
Background generation outcomes delivered while a project is closed
Headless or hybrid gateway writes interleaved with renderer delivery
internal_only_reason: The intent boundary and project persistence ownership are application invariants; external reconciliation systems do not decide Nomi Run binding or project schema semantics.
invariants: Only explicit delete gestures and their undo/redo projection emit production detach or reattach signals.
Project canvas writes are serialized by projectId in the main process and re-read current state inside the write queue.
Renderer delivery never saves a whole project record directly; it calls the main applyCanvasNodePatch port.
Loading, unloading, switching projects, and ordinary non-production creation undo emit no production signal.
Every production canvas signal carries the projectId held by the emitting canvas store; history replay preserves it and a host drops mismatches with a warning.

Canvas content and project identity are installed in one load commit; an empty-identity production signal is logged with node/document identity diagnostics and dropped, while production-node insertion paths reject missing identity.

door_reduction.why_not: The fixed boundary keeps every existing deletion and project-write door and adds the project-scoped signal router plus the load-commit identity invariant; signal producers, journal replay, and the host remain separate doors because they own creation, persistence, and consumption respectively.

generality_proof: Every listed deletion caller converges on the canvas store actions or document commit before a production signal can be emitted, while every project canvas disk writer converges on serializeProjectCanvasWrite. A future caller cannot silently infer a delete or write around the boundary without adding a new door that the door map exposes.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Records the explicit production signal intent on the active history gesture so undo inverts it and redo replays it without snapshot-diff inference.
Carries explicit production detach/reattach intent and has no snapshot-diff inference.
Serializes all main-process project canvas writes by projectId and reads current state inside the queue.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Undo and redo replay the history record signal intent (undo inverted); external whole-graph writes record explicit action-time deltas, and load paths do not call it.
Closed-project outcomes use the main applyCanvasNodePatch port and no renderer save function.
Project load establishes a baseline and intentionally emits no production signal.

recurrence.reason: Any new delete gesture or project writer could otherwise repeat the inference or interleaving failure.

prevention.invariant: Every production signal is project-scoped and only a matching host may invoke the main-process queue; the queue commits a project canvas write and patches current state inside the queue.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing project, node, identity binding, or write port fails closed without saving a stale whole record.
prevention.strategy: Move renderer delivery to an IPC patch and share one main queue with gateway writes; make delete intent an explicit signal at the canvas write boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: Snapshot-diff deletion inference and renderer whole-record saving are deleted rather than retained as fallback paths.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant belongs to Nomi's canvas and project persistence boundaries.

migration: Project file shape and existing canvas data are unchanged; only the writer path and signal source change. Existing sessions load normally and establish a baseline without emitting production commands.
residual_risks: Real packaged Electron multi-window verification is unverified.
A production node deleted and never undone remains detached by design; its Run result remains durable.
External project writers outside this Electron main process are not coordinated by this in-process queue.
